warnings: Density curves sampled at 100 points instead of 200 to keep the response under the 100,000-byte contract (# bytes at 200); every point is the exact fitted Gaussian.

Each slice's energy axis runs from 0 to the 99th percentile of the series that set it plus 5%, or to their largest value where they are too few for percentiles, rounded out to whole ticks; 22 of 572 values lie beyond their slice's axis (5–6 GeV: 4; 13–14 GeV: 4; 14–15 GeV: 8; 16–17 GeV: 6) and are excluded from the view but not from the statistics.

Below the 15-shower histogram floor: 5–6 GeV (Shower B); 9–10 GeV (Shower A); 12–13 GeV (Shower A); 13–14 GeV (Shower B); 14–15 GeV (Shower B); 16–17 GeV (Shower B); 17–18 GeV (Shower A). μ and σ there are plain sample moments (ddof = 1) rather than core refits, quoted with their standard errors; the density histogram is suppressed because at this sample size it is a comb of bin-width spikes, and these curves do not set the density axis.

momentum_marker.mean: Mean incident momentum p of the slice's showers (GeV).
momentum_marker.sd: Sample SD of p (ddof = 1): an uncapped band, √N wider than the whisker.

ci95.label: 95% Student-t interval of the mean p (N − 1 d.o.f.): a capped whisker.

sd_ci95.label: 95% χ² interval of the SD (N − 1 d.o.f.), asymmetric.

message.curve+strip: the density histogram is suppressed - at this sample size it would be a comb of spikes whose heights are set by the bin width rather than by physics. The individual events, the mean with its 95% confidence interval and the sample dispersion are drawn instead, and mu and sigma are reported in the table with their own uncertainty.
message.strip: below the 8-event floor for a continuous density curve. A smooth curve from this few events would assert a shape the sample cannot constrain, so only the events and the summary markers are drawn. mu and sigma are still reported, with their uncertainty.
message.degenerate: all at one energy to floating-point precision. The width is a measured zero rather than an unknown, and no density curve is drawn: a delta is not a density and would put an unbounded spike on the axis.

estimator_note.moments: μ and σ are plain sample moments (ddof = 1), σ quoted with its standard error and its χ² 95% interval; no core refit below the 15-event floor, so a curve, where drawn, is de-weighted and does not set the axis scale.
estimator_note.moments_1dof: μ and σ are plain sample moments (ddof = 1); σ is one pairwise difference (1 d.o.f.), quoted with its χ² 95% interval.
estimator_note.mean_only: A single event fixes a position and nothing else; no width exists to report.
estimator_note.degenerate: Every event shares one energy: the width is a measured zero, not an unknown.
